l.i: Quippe tuos (confide) pedes, captiuáque membra
Venantum expediet laqueis & compede trifti.
Ipse tuos humerorum umbra circumteget artus,
Ipsius & clypeo tua spes haerebit & alis:
Ut neque te spectris nocturna volantibus umbra,
Sole nec exorto iaculorum terreat imber,
Nec media vaga nocte lues, nec luce ferena
Exitiale malum: non fi tibi dextera mille
Mille finiftra cadant celeri data corpora letho:
Quin fcelerum poenas & praemia digna ferentes Securus, custode Deo, spectabis acervos.
Nánque Deus mea spes, mea fola potestia, dixti.
Ergo nulla tuis accedent vulnera teftis.
Quippe incedentem Domini mandata secuta
Angelica cingent acies hinc semper & illinc.
Quinetiam ne faxa pedem remorentur euntis, S-
uscipient, tenerisque ferent tua membra lacertis.
Cadetur tibi calce Draco, catulíque leæna,
Aspide cum dura, rigidíque impune leones:
Sincero, Deus inquit, enim me amplexus amore
est: Nominis ille mei non infcius. Ergo, ait, illum
Omnibus eripiam terráque marique periclis.
Si mea supplicibus veneretur Numina votis,
Annuam, & afflictis tribuam folatia rebus.
Quin & longinqua producam tempora vitæ:
Ille falute mea tandem & fine fine fruetur.

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "noële" in "nocte" (line 7 of second half, marked as read), "fpes" read as "spes", "Ipsius" and "Mille" lines are as printed. The poem's word divisions and stanza breaks are inferred from indentation and sense; the stanza breaks may differ slightly. Faint mirrored text in the right margin is show-through and omitted. The catchword "PSAL-" is at the lower right.
